idea.body: A remainder means something different depending on the story. If 23 seeds are packed into bags of 5, the remainder 3 is just what is left over, sitting outside any full bag. If 23 people need vans that hold 5 each, that leftover 3 still needs a whole van. Round up to 5 vans, not 4. If a recipe only cares about full bags, the leftover is set aside and you round down to 4 bags. The same division, three different answers, because the question decides whether you want the remainder, the quotient, or the quotient rounded up.

workedExample.prompt: A robot's crate holds 34 bolts, packed into bags of 6. How many bags are needed to hold every bolt, with none left uncovered?
steps: 34 divided by 6 gives a quotient of 5 and a remainder of 4.
5 bags hold 30 bolts, leaving 4 bolts uncovered.
Those 4 bolts still need a bag of their own, even though the bag is not full.
Round the quotient up: 6 bags are needed in total.

ways.name: Leftover as the answer
ways.when: Use this when the question only cares about what does not fit in a full set.
steps: Divide 23 by 5: the quotient is 4, since 5 times 4 is 20.
The leftover 3 is the answer, sitting outside any full bag.
ways.example: 23 seeds into bags of 5, seeds left over
ways.trap: Reporting the quotient, 4, instead of the leftover, 3.

ways.name: Round the quotient up
ways.when: Use this when every leftover item still needs a whole container of its own.
steps: Divide 34 by 6: the quotient is 5, remainder 4.
5 full bags hold 30 bolts, leaving 4 bolts uncovered.
Those 4 bolts still need a bag of their own.
Round the quotient up: 5 plus 1 is 6 bags.
ways.example: 34 bolts into bags of 6, bags needed for every bolt
ways.trap: Stopping at the quotient, 5, and forgetting the leftover bolts need a bag too.

ways.name: Round the quotient down
ways.when: Use this when only full, complete groups count toward the answer.
steps: Divide 29 by 6: the quotient is 4, remainder 5.
The 5 leftover eggs do not make a full carton.
Only count the full cartons and set the leftover aside.
The answer is the quotient itself: 4 full cartons.
ways.example: 29 eggs into cartons of 6, full cartons only
ways.trap: Rounding up by mistake and counting a carton that is not actually full.
